cards.front: How are the primary skin lesions named by shape, size and content?
cards.back: Flat: **macule** (<1 cm), **patch** (>1 cm). Raised and solid: **papule** (<1 cm), **plaque** (>1 cm, flat-topped), **nodule** (deeper, >1 cm). Fluid-filled: **vesicle** (<1 cm), **bulla** (>1 cm). **Pustule**: a raised lesion filled with pus.
cards.back_pt: Planas: **mácula** (<1 cm), **mancha** (>1 cm). Elevadas e sólidas: **pápula** (<1 cm), **placa** (>1 cm, de topo plano), **nódulo** (mais profundo, >1 cm). Com líquido: **vesícula** (<1 cm), **bolha** (>1 cm). **Pústula**: lesão elevada com pus.

cards.front: What is the Nikolsky sign, and in which diseases is it positive?
cards.back: Light rubbing makes normal-looking epidermis **separate and slide off**. The epidermis itself is fragile: cells have lost their junctions, or the whole layer is necrotic. Positive in **pemphigus vulgaris**, **staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome** and **SJS/TEN**; negative in **bullous pemphigoid** (intact epidermis).
cards.back_pt: A fricção leve da pele de aspecto normal faz a epiderme **se descolar e deslizar**. Indica que a própria epiderme está frágil: suas células perderam as junções, ou toda a camada está necrótica. Positivo no **pênfigo vulgar**, na **síndrome da pele escaldada estafilocócica** e na **SSJ/NET**; negativo no **penfigoide bolhoso** (epiderme íntegra).

cards.front: Where does atopic dermatitis appear at different ages, and what barrier defect is linked to it?
cards.back: Itchy, dry, eczematous skin on the **cheeks and extensor surfaces** in infants, and in the **flexures** (front of elbows, back of knees) in older children and adults. **Filaggrin** gene defects weaken the skin barrier. Often occurs with **asthma** and **allergic rhinitis**.
cards.back_pt: Pele seca, pruriginosa e eczematosa nas **bochechas e superfícies extensoras** no lactente, e nas **flexuras** (fossas antecubitais e poplíteas) em crianças maiores e adultos. Defeitos no gene da **filagrina** enfraquecem a barreira cutânea. Costuma ocorrer com **asma** e **rinite alérgica**.

cards.front: How does allergic contact dermatitis differ from irritant contact dermatitis?
cards.back: **Allergic**: **type IV** (T-cell) hypersensitivity in a person sensitized before, e.g., to **nickel**, **poison ivy** or neomycin. Itchy vesicles appear 1-3 days after contact, in the shape of the contact area. **Irritant**: direct chemical damage (soaps, solvents); no sensitization needed.
cards.back_pt: **Alérgica**: hipersensibilidade **tipo IV** (mediada por linfócitos T) em pessoa já sensibilizada, ex.: **níquel**, **hera venenosa** (*poison ivy*) ou neomicina. Vesículas pruriginosas surgem 1-3 dias após o contato, no formato da área de contato. **Irritativa**: lesão química direta (sabões, solventes); não exige sensibilização.

cards.front: What are the clinical and histologic features of lichen planus?
cards.back: Itchy, **purple, polygonal, flat-topped papules and plaques** (the "6 Ps"), often with fine white lines (**Wickham striae**). Histology: a **band-like lymphocytic infiltrate** at the dermal-epidermal junction with **sawtooth** rete ridges. Linked to **hepatitis C**.
cards.back_pt: **Pápulas e placas pruriginosas, violáceas, poligonais e planas** (os "6 Ps" em inglês), muitas vezes com finas linhas brancas (**estrias de Wickham**). Histologia: **infiltrado linfocitário em faixa** na junção dermoepidérmica, com cristas epidérmicas **em dente de serra**. Associado à **hepatite C**.

cards.front: How do SJS and TEN differ, and which drugs classically cause them?
cards.back: One disease spectrum: **full-thickness epidermal necrosis** with mucosal involvement and a positive Nikolsky sign. Detached skin: **SJS** <10% of body surface, **overlap** 10-30%, **TEN** >30%. Classic drugs: **allopurinol**, **carbamazepine** (and other aromatic anticonvulsants), **sulfonamides** and lamotrigine.
cards.back_pt: Um mesmo espectro: **necrose epidérmica de espessura total** com acometimento de mucosas e sinal de Nikolsky positivo. Pele descolada: **SSJ** <10% da superfície corporal, **sobreposição** 10-30%, **NET** >30%. Fármacos clássicos: **alopurinol**, **carbamazepina** (e outros anticonvulsivantes aromáticos), **sulfonamidas** e lamotrigina.

cards.front: How does hereditary angioedema differ from allergic urticaria?
cards.back: **Urticaria**: itchy **wheals** from **mast cell** degranulation (histamine); each wheal fades within 24 hours. **Hereditary angioedema**: **C1 inhibitor** deficiency; **bradykinin** causes deep swelling **without wheals or itch** and no response to antihistamines.
cards.back_pt: **Urticária**: **urticas** pruriginosas por degranulação de **mastócitos** (histamina); cada urtica some em até 24 horas. **Angioedema hereditário**: deficiência do **inibidor de C1**; a **bradicinina** causa edema profundo **sem urticas nem prurido** e sem resposta a anti-histamínicos.

cards.front: What is erythema nodosum, and which conditions cause it?
cards.back: Tender red **nodules** on the **shins**. Histology: **septal panniculitis** (inflammation of the fat septa) without vasculitis. Causes: **streptococcal infection**, **sarcoidosis**, **IBD**, **tuberculosis**, **coccidioidomycosis**, and estrogen (pregnancy, oral contraceptives); many cases are idiopathic.
cards.back_pt: **Nódulos** eritematosos e dolorosos nas **regiões pré-tibiais**. Histologia: **paniculite septal** (inflamação dos septos do tecido adiposo) sem vasculite. Causas: **infecção estreptocócica**, **sarcoidose**, **DII**, **tuberculose**, **coccidioidomicose** e estrogênio (gestação, anticoncepcionais orais); muitos casos são idiopáticos.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had painful mouth sores for 2 months. Over the last 3 weeks, soft, thin-walled blisters have appeared on her chest and back. They break easily and leave raw, red erosions. Light rubbing of normal-looking skin near a blister makes the top layer slide off. A skin biopsy shows a blister just above the basal layer; the basal cells stay attached to the basement membrane. Direct immunofluorescence shows IgG around each keratinocyte in a net-like pattern. Her autoantibodies most likely target which protein?
choices: BP180 (type XVII collagen) of hemidesmosomes
Type VII collagen of anchoring fibrils
Desmoglein 3 of desmosomes
Epidermal transglutaminase
Keratin 5 and 14 of basal cells
questions.explanation: Oral erosions, flaccid bullae, a positive **Nikolsky sign**, **suprabasal acantholysis** and **net-like intercellular IgG** point to **pemphigus vulgaris**. IgG attacks **desmoglein 3** (and often desmoglein 1), so keratinocytes lose their connections to each other. BP180 is the target in bullous pemphigoid, which gives tense subepidermal blisters, linear IgG along the basement membrane and a negative Nikolsky sign.
questions.explanation_pt: Erosões orais, bolhas flácidas, **sinal de Nikolsky** positivo, **acantólise suprabasal** e **IgG intercelular em rede** indicam **pênfigo vulgar**. A IgG ataca a **desmogleína 3** (e muitas vezes a desmogleína 1), e os queratinócitos perdem a ligação entre si. O BP180 é o alvo no penfigoide bolhoso, que causa bolhas tensas subepidérmicas, IgG linear ao longo da membrana basal e sinal de Nikolsky negativo.

questions.stem: An 81-year-old man has had itchy skin for several months. Now he has tense, fluid-filled blisters, 1 to 3 cm wide, on red, hive-like plaques on his inner thighs, groin and the flexor side of his forearms. His mouth is normal. Rubbing normal-looking skin does not detach it. A biopsy shows a blister below the epidermis with many eosinophils. Direct immunofluorescence shows a linear band of IgG and C3 along the basement membrane. His autoantibodies most likely target which structure?
choices: Desmosomes that link keratinocytes to each other
Hemidesmosomes that anchor basal keratinocytes to the basement membrane
Keratin filaments inside basal keratinocytes
Tight junctions in the stratum granulosum
Desmosomes of the upper epidermis only (desmoglein 1)
questions.explanation: An older patient with itchy, **tense bullae** on urticarial plaques, no oral lesions, a **negative Nikolsky sign**, a **subepidermal** blister rich in eosinophils and **linear IgG and C3** at the basement membrane has **bullous pemphigoid**. IgG targets **hemidesmosomal proteins (BP180 and BP230)**, so the whole epidermis lifts off the dermis and the blister roof stays thick. Antibodies against desmosomes (pemphigus vulgaris) split the epidermis itself, cause flaccid blisters and oral erosions, and give net-like intercellular staining.
questions.explanation_pt: Paciente idoso com **bolhas tensas** pruriginosas sobre placas urticariformes, sem lesões orais, **sinal de Nikolsky negativo**, bolha **subepidérmica** rica em eosinófilos e **IgG e C3 lineares** na membrana basal tem **penfigoide bolhoso**. A IgG ataca **proteínas dos hemidesmossomos (BP180 e BP230)**, e toda a epiderme se descola da derme, com teto da bolha espesso. Anticorpos contra desmossomos (pênfigo vulgar) separam a própria epiderme, causam bolhas flácidas e erosões orais e dão marcação intercelular em rede.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy is brought in for a sports physical. His BMI is 35 kg/m2. The skin on the back of his neck and in both axillae is dark brown, thick and velvety. It does not wash off. He has no itching. Fasting plasma glucose is 108 mg/dL, and fasting insulin is high. Which mechanism best explains his skin finding?
choices: High insulin levels stimulate IGF-1 receptors on keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts
High ACTH levels stimulate melanocortin-1 receptors on melanocytes
Autoimmune T cells destroy melanocytes in the basal layer
Overgrowth of Malassezia yeast in the stratum corneum
Type IV hypersensitivity to a chemical in a skin-care product
questions.explanation: Velvety, hyperpigmented, thickened skin in the neck and axillae is **acanthosis nigricans**. In obesity, **insulin resistance** causes **hyperinsulinemia**, and insulin at high levels activates **IGF-1 receptors**, so keratinocytes and fibroblasts proliferate. ACTH-driven hyperpigmentation (primary adrenal insufficiency) is diffuse and is most visible in palmar creases, knuckles, scars and the gums; it does not make the skin thick and velvety. Sudden, widespread acanthosis nigricans in an older, thin adult should raise concern for an internal cancer, most often **gastric adenocarcinoma**.
questions.explanation_pt: Pele aveludada, hiperpigmentada e espessada no pescoço e nas axilas é **acantose nigricante**. Na obesidade, a **resistência à insulina** causa **hiperinsulinemia**, e a insulina em níveis altos ativa **receptores de IGF-1**, levando à proliferação de queratinócitos e fibroblastos. A hiperpigmentação por ACTH (insuficiência adrenal primária) é difusa e mais visível nas linhas palmares, nas articulações dos dedos, em cicatrizes e nas gengivas; não deixa a pele espessa e aveludada. Uma acantose nigricante súbita e extensa em adulto mais velho e magro deve levantar suspeita de câncer interno, mais frequentemente **adenocarcinoma gástrico**.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has had scaly skin lesions for 2 years. Exam shows sharply defined, red plaques with thick silvery-white scale on both elbows, both knees and the scalp. When a scale is scraped off, small bleeding points appear. A new plaque has formed along a recent scratch on his forearm. Several fingernails have small pits. A skin biopsy is done. Which finding is most likely?
choices: Spongiosis with fluid between keratinocytes in the epidermis
Suprabasal acantholysis with intact basal cells
Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermal-epidermal junction
Parakeratosis with collections of neutrophils in the stratum corneum
Granular IgA deposits at the tips of the dermal papillae
questions.explanation: Silvery-scaled plaques on extensor surfaces, pinpoint bleeding when scale is removed (**Auspitz sign**), new lesions at sites of trauma (**Koebner phenomenon**) and **nail pitting** mean **psoriasis**. The epidermis is thick, with **parakeratosis** (nuclei kept in the stratum corneum) and neutrophil collections called **Munro microabscesses**; the suprapapillary plates are thin and dilated capillaries sit at the tops of long dermal papillae, which explains the bleeding points. Lichen planus also shows the Koebner phenomenon and has a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, but its lesions are purple, flat-topped papules without thick silvery scale.
questions.explanation_pt: Placas com escamas prateadas em superfícies extensoras, pontos de sangramento ao remover a escama (**sinal de Auspitz**), novas lesões em locais de trauma (**fenômeno de Koebner**) e **depressões ungueais** (*nail pitting*) indicam **psoríase**. A epiderme é espessa, com **paraceratose** (núcleos retidos na camada córnea) e coleções de neutrófilos chamadas **microabscessos de Munro**; as placas suprapapilares são finas e há capilares dilatados no topo de papilas dérmicas alongadas, o que explica os pontos de sangramento. O líquen plano também apresenta fenômeno de Koebner e tem infiltrado linfocitário em faixa, mas suas lesões são pápulas violáceas de topo plano, sem escamas prateadas espessas.

notes.title: Inflammatory skin disease: patterns, blisters and clues
notes.body_md:
## Secondary lesion words

- **Scale**: flakes of stratum corneum. **Crust**: dried serum or blood.
- **Erosion**: partial loss of epidermis; heals without a scar. **Ulcer**: loss into the dermis; may scar.

## Eczema and scaly rashes

- **Atopic dermatitis**: filaggrin defect; **spongiosis** on biopsy.
- **Contact dermatitis**: allergic is type IV; irritant is direct damage.
- **Seborrheic dermatitis**: greasy yellow scale on scalp, eyebrows and nasolabial folds; linked to *Malassezia*; *cradle cap* in infants; severe in HIV and Parkinson disease.
- **Psoriasis**: silvery plaques on extensors; **Auspitz sign**, **Koebner phenomenon**, **nail pitting**.
- **Lichen planus**: purple flat papules; hepatitis C.
- **Pityriasis rosea**: one **herald patch**, then oval scaly patches along skin lines (*Christmas tree* pattern); resolves alone.

## Follicles

- **Acne vulgaris**: androgens raise sebum, follicles plug (**comedones**), *Cutibacterium acnes* drives inflammation.
- **Rosacea**: central facial flushing, telangiectasias, papules and pustules, **no comedones**; late **rhinophyma**.
- **Hidradenitis suppurativa**: painful nodules, abscesses and **sinus tracts** in axillae and groin; scars.

## Reactive patterns

- **Erythema multiforme**: **target lesions**, often on palms and soles; most often after **HSV**.
- **SJS/TEN**: drug-induced epidermal necrosis.
- **Erythema nodosum**: septal panniculitis on the shins.

## Blistering diseases

- **Pemphigus vulgaris**: IgG to **desmoglein**; intraepidermal; flaccid bullae, oral erosions, Nikolsky positive.
- **Bullous pemphigoid**: IgG to **BP180** (hemidesmosome); subepidermal; tense bullae in older adults; Nikolsky negative.
- **Dermatitis herpetiformis**: granular IgA; **celiac disease** (see GI).

## Pigment and hair

- **Vitiligo**: autoimmune loss of melanocytes; sharp white patches.
- **Alopecia areata**: T cells attack hair follicles; round, non-scarring bald patches.
- **Acanthosis nigricans**: velvety dark folds; **insulin resistance**; sudden onset in an older adult suggests **gastric adenocarcinoma**.

Topical drug facts: see musculoskeletal-dermatology pharmacology.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Termos de lesões secundárias

- **Escama**: lâminas da camada córnea. **Crosta**: soro ou sangue ressecado.
- **Erosão**: perda parcial da epiderme; cura sem deixar cicatriz. **Úlcera**: perda que atinge a derme; pode deixar cicatriz.

## Eczemas e erupções descamativas

- **Dermatite atópica**: defeito da filagrina; **espongiose** na biópsia.
- **Dermatite de contato**: a alérgica é tipo IV; a irritativa é lesão direta.
- **Dermatite seborreica**: escamas amareladas e oleosas no couro cabeludo, sobrancelhas e sulcos nasogenianos; ligada à *Malassezia*; *crosta láctea* no lactente; grave no HIV e na doença de Parkinson.
- **Psoríase**: placas prateadas em extensores; **sinal de Auspitz**, **fenômeno de Koebner**, **depressões ungueais** (*nail pitting*).
- **Líquen plano**: pápulas planas violáceas; hepatite C.
- **Pitiríase rósea**: uma **placa-mãe** (medalhão; *herald patch*), depois manchas ovais descamativas ao longo das linhas da pele (padrão em *árvore de Natal*); regride sozinha.

## Folículos

- **Acne vulgar**: andrógenos aumentam o sebo, os folículos se obstruem (**comedões**) e o *Cutibacterium acnes* promove inflamação.
- **Rosácea**: rubor facial central, telangiectasias, pápulas e pústulas, **sem comedões**; tardiamente **rinofima**.
- **Hidradenite supurativa**: nódulos dolorosos, abscessos e **trajetos fistulosos** em axilas e virilhas; cicatrizes.

## Padrões reativos

- **Eritema multiforme**: **lesões em alvo**, muitas vezes em palmas e plantas; mais frequentemente após **HSV**.
- **SSJ/NET**: necrose epidérmica induzida por fármacos.
- **Eritema nodoso**: paniculite septal nas regiões pré-tibiais.

## Doenças bolhosas

- **Pênfigo vulgar**: IgG contra **desmogleína**; intraepidérmico; bolhas flácidas, erosões orais, Nikolsky positivo.
- **Penfigoide bolhoso**: IgG contra **BP180** (hemidesmossomo); subepidérmico; bolhas tensas em idosos; Nikolsky negativo.
- **Dermatite herpetiforme**: IgA granular; **doença celíaca** (ver GI).

## Pigmento e pelos

- **Vitiligo**: perda autoimune de melanócitos; manchas brancas bem delimitadas.
- **Alopecia areata**: linfócitos T atacam os folículos pilosos; placas redondas de alopecia não cicatricial.
- **Acantose nigricante**: dobras escurecidas e aveludadas; **resistência à insulina**; início súbito em adulto mais velho sugere **adenocarcinoma gástrico**.

Fármacos tópicos: ver farmacologia musculoesquelética e dermatológica.
